name: building-ramp-visual
description: #555: ordering a ramp queues progressive dig_ramp_segment excavation work instead of carving the whole corridor instantly. A staffed, excavator-crewed rock_digger digs a 6-segment ramp one segment at a time — this scenario screenshots the corridor half-dug (orderedRampSegmentCount:3) and again once every segment has landed (orderedRampSegmentCount:0), proving the dig happens incrementally rather than in one synchronous burst.

steps.description: Staffed vehicles come unmanned (#551) — crew rock_digger #3 with driver #4, the first of the two driving.excavator-qualified drivers STARTING_SITE_STAFFED_COMPOSITION grants (balance.ts), before ordering any excavation work.
Order the ramp — order-time validates and charges the whole corridor, then queues one dig_ramp_segment PendingAction per segment (#555) instead of carving anything yet.

expect.note: 6 segments ordered (one per length-step, entrance-first), none carved yet.

steps.description: Drain half the ordered segments — the crewed rock_digger digs one dig_ramp_segment action at a time, nearest/entrance-first (mirrors #553's drill_hole landing order). This step's own auto-captured screenshot is the mid-dig checkpoint: the corridor is carved partway down, not the whole length.

expect.note: Mid-dig: half of the ramp's 6 segments have landed, half remain queued.

steps.description: Drain the remaining segments. This step's own auto-captured screenshot is the full-completion checkpoint: every segment carved, the ramp corridor complete end to end.

expect.note: Ramp fully dug: every dig_ramp_segment action landed.
